title: Critical Reasoning in Verbal Context
tagline: Year 3 — Main conclusions, hidden assumptions, flaws, paradoxes and parallel reasoning in short arguments

introduction.overview: Verbal critical reasoning treats a short passage as an argument. You are asked to find the conclusion, name the assumption, spot a flaw, resolve an apparent contradiction, or pick an argument with the same pattern. All of these start with the same step: separate the conclusion from its supporting statements, then look at the gap between them. Every question type is a different question about that gap.
introduction.placementRelevance: These items appear in the verbal sections of management and campus tests alongside reading comprehension.
introduction.realWorldContext: Assessing a proposal, a news story or an advertisement uses the same questions.

learningObjectives: Identify necessary assumptions with the negation test
Name common flaws (correlation, sample, converse, false cause)
Resolve paradoxes with a reconciling fact

requiredTopics: Critical Reasoning — Strengthen and Weaken Arguments
prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A conclusion is signalled by words like therefore, thus, so, should; premises by because, since, given that.

coreDefinitions: Main conclusion: the claim the rest of the argument supports.
Assumption: an unstated premise the argument needs.
Flaw: an error in the way premises are used to reach the conclusion.
Paradox: two facts that seem to conflict; a resolution gives a fact that makes both true.
Parallel reasoning: another argument with the same logical form, valid or flawed.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Every question is about the same skeleton: premises, a gap, a conclusion. Find the skeleton, then ask which question is being asked of it.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Mark the conclusion. List the premises. State the gap in one line. Then answer the specific question: what fills the gap (assumption), what is wrong with it (flaw), what follows (inference), what explains it (paradox).

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Negation test
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Deny the assumption; the argument fails

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Common flaws
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Correlation as cause; unrepresentative sample; converse; part-whole

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Paradox resolver
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: A fact that explains both observations

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Parallel form
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Copy the logical shape, not the topic
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: No A is B; all C are B; no C is A

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Must be true
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Some books on the top shelf

mainNarrative: To find the main conclusion, look for the recommendation or claim the rest supports. In "Our town's bus service loses money, and passengers are falling. Raising fares will only drive away more passengers. The council should therefore improve the frequency of buses instead", the conclusion is the final sentence. The rest are premises.

An assumption is a bridge. "The school banned phones so that students will pay more attention" assumes that students will pay more attention if phones are not available. Negate it and the ban has no point.

Common flaws: "The last three managers who wore blue ties were promoted, so blue ties lead to promotion" confuses correlation with cause. "No one has proved the product is not the best, so it is the best" treats absence of disproof as proof.

To resolve a paradox, find a fact that makes both observations true. A hospital introduced a scheduling system to cut waiting times, yet waits rose. If the easier booking system brought many more patients, both facts hold.

For parallel reasoning, rewrite each argument in symbols. "No dog is a bird; all sparrows are birds; so no sparrow is a dog" has the form No A is B; all C are B; so no C is A. A hammer-tool-toy argument with the same form is parallel.

deepDiveAspects.title: Converse error
deepDiveAspects.content: All A are B does not give All B are A; "Ravi is educated, so he is a professor" is invalid.

deepDiveAspects.title: Sampling flaw
deepDiveAspects.content: Surveying only people leaving a gym tells you about gym-goers, not about people in general.

solvedExamples.title: Main conclusion
solvedExamples.question: A town's bus service loses money and passengers are falling; raising fares would drive more away. "The council should therefore improve bus frequency instead." Which sentence is the conclusion?

steps.title: Content
steps.explanation: Improve bus frequency instead of raising fares.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: The council should improve bus frequency instead of raising fares

solvedExamples.title: Flaw
solvedExamples.question: The last three managers who wore blue ties were promoted, so wearing a blue tie leads to promotion. What is the flaw?

steps.title: Flaw
steps.explanation: It assumes the first caused the second.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: It assumes that a connection between two events shows that one causes the other

solvedExamples.title: Paradox
solvedExamples.question: A hospital introduced a scheduling system to cut waiting times, yet waiting times rose. What resolves this?

steps.title: Look for
steps.explanation: A fact that makes both true.

steps.title: Fact
steps.explanation: Easier booking brought many more patients.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: The new system made booking easier, so many more patients came
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The system worked but demand grew.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Mark the conclusion, list the premises, state the gap, and only then read the options with the question type in mind.

commonMistakes.mistake: Picking a premise as the conclusion
Choosing an assumption that is too strong

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that are extreme, irrelevant or restate the premise.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: For parallel reasoning, replace nouns with letters.

easy.question:
Argument: Every employee of the firm who works night shifts is paid an allowance. Rakesh works night shifts.

Which of the following must be true if the statements above are true?
options: All employees of the firm are paid an allowance.
Rakesh is paid an allowance.
Rakesh works more hours than the others.
Rakesh prefers night shifts.
easy.explanation: The first statement applies to every night-shift employee, so Rakesh is paid the allowance. The other options go beyond the statements.

easy.question:
Argument: The town's bus service loses money every year and the number of passengers is falling. Raising fares will only drive away more passengers. The council should therefore improve the frequency of buses instead.

Which of the following is the main conclusion of the argument?
options: The council should improve the frequency of buses instead of raising fares.
The town's bus service loses money every year.
The number of passengers is falling.
Raising fares will drive away more passengers.
easy.correctAnswer: The council should improve the frequency of buses instead of raising fares.
easy.explanation: The word "therefore" marks the conclusion; the other statements are premises.

easy.question:
Argument: A school has banned mobile phones in classrooms so that students will pay more attention to lessons.

Which of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?
options: All students own mobile phones.
Teachers dislike phones.
Phones are expensive to replace.
Students will pay more attention if phones are not available in class.
easy.correctAnswer: Students will pay more attention if phones are not available in class.
easy.explanation: The ban is meant to improve attention, which works only if removing phones increases attention.

intermediate.question:
Argument: The new software cut the time taken to process an invoice from ten minutes to four, so the finance team will be able to process more invoices each day.

Which of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?
options: The time saved will be used to process more invoices.
The software is cheaper than the old system.
Invoices will become simpler.
The finance team will be given a bonus.
intermediate.correctAnswer: The time saved will be used to process more invoices.
intermediate.explanation: The conclusion that more invoices will be processed depends on the saved time actually being used for processing.

intermediate.question:
Argument: The last three managers who wore blue ties were promoted, so wearing a blue tie leads to promotion.

The reasoning in the argument is flawed because it
options: relies on the opinion of an expert
uses a very large sample
contradicts one of its own premises
assumes that two events occurring together means that one causes the other
intermediate.correctAnswer: assumes that two events occurring together means that one causes the other
intermediate.explanation: Three cases where two things coincide do not show that a blue tie causes promotion.

intermediate.question:
Argument: Online courses are better than classroom courses, because students enrolled in them score higher in the final exams.

Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Online courses are cheaper than classroom courses.
Final exams are held in classrooms.
Many students enjoy online courses.
Students who choose online courses are generally those who already had higher marks before enrolling.
intermediate.correctAnswer: Students who choose online courses are generally those who already had higher marks before enrolling.
intermediate.explanation: If online students were stronger to begin with, their higher scores need not result from the courses.

advanced.question:
Argument: A survey of people leaving a gym found that 90 per cent exercised regularly. The researcher concluded that most people in the city exercise regularly.

The reasoning in the argument is flawed because it
options: uses too many people in the survey
ignores that exercise is healthy
confuses a cause with its effect
bases a general claim on a sample that is not representative
advanced.correctAnswer: bases a general claim on a sample that is not representative
advanced.explanation: People leaving a gym are more likely than others to exercise, so the sample is not representative of the city.

advanced.question:
Argument: A college argues that its teaching is superior, because 95 per cent of its graduates found jobs within six months.

Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: The college has a large library.
Some graduates started their own businesses.
The college admits only students with very high prior marks and strong family business connections.
The college has been open for fifty years.
advanced.correctAnswer: The college admits only students with very high prior marks and strong family business connections.
advanced.explanation: High-scoring, well-connected students may find jobs regardless of teaching, giving another explanation for the placement record.

placementStyle.question:
Argument: Since the state taxed sugary drinks, sales of these drinks have fallen by 20 per cent. The health minister concludes that the tax has improved public health.

Which of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?
options: All consumers know the dangers of sugary drinks.
Consumers who bought fewer sugary drinks did not switch to other equally unhealthy products.
The tax is the highest in the country.
Sales of other drinks have not changed.
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Consumers who bought fewer sugary drinks did not switch to other equally unhealthy products.
placementStyle.explanation: If people switched to equally unhealthy products, health would not improve, so the argument needs that they did not.

placementStyle.question:
Argument: All professors are educated. Ravi is educated. Therefore Ravi is a professor.

Which of the following arguments contains the same flaw?
options: All footballers are fit. Sameer is a footballer. Therefore Sameer is fit.
All footballers are fit. Sameer is fit. Therefore Sameer is a footballer.
No footballer is lazy. Sameer is a footballer. Therefore Sameer is not lazy.
All footballers are fit. Sameer is not fit. Therefore Sameer is not a footballer.
placementStyle.correctAnswer: All footballers are fit. Sameer is fit. Therefore Sameer is a footballer.
placementStyle.explanation: Both reason from "all A are B" and "x is B" to "x is A", which is the converse error. The other options are valid.

placementStyle.question:
Argument: No member of the club who pays dues late is allowed to vote. Some members who are allowed to vote hold office.

Which of the following must be true if the statements above are true?
options: Some office-holders of the club do not pay dues late.
All office-holders are allowed to vote.
No office-holder pays dues late.
Some members who pay dues late hold office and vote.
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Some office-holders of the club do not pay dues late.
placementStyle.explanation: The voting members who hold office are allowed to vote, so they do not pay late; hence some office-holders do not pay late.
